name: server/mzizi-mongodb
title: mzizi-mongodb
summary: A read-only MongoDB client over the wire protocol (OP_MSG, SCRAM-SHA-256, a small BSON codec), sans-IO, for places the official driver cannot build, such as a Cloudflare Worker.

surface.summary: One authenticated connection over a byte transport.
Documents matching a filter, at most MAX_FIND_DOCS.
The first matching document, if any.
A pipeline's results, at most MAX_AGGREGATE_DOCS; $out and $merge refused.
SCRAM-SHA-256 with a caller-supplied nonce, so the core stays pure.
Report each command and refusal to a server harness.

limits.summary: The most documents one find returns.
The most documents one aggregation returns; more is an error, not a silent cut.

guarantees.statement: There is no write path: the client offers find, find_one and aggregate, and aggregate refuses a pipeline containing $out or $merge before anything is sent.

A find is capped at MAX_FIND_DOCS (and at its own limit, even against a server that ignores it), carries a server-side time limit and read preference secondaryPreferred; an aggregation past MAX_AGGREGATE_DOCS, in one batch or many, kills its cursor and is refused.
A database or collection name outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,120} is refused before any bytes are sent.
Authentication completes only against a real SCRAM-SHA-256 exchange, fails on a wrong password, and refuses a server that cannot prove it knows the password.
Malformed BSON, a malformed wire header, a reply to another request and a hostile SCRAM message are errors, never panics.
The password never appears in a Debug string or an error message.

A pooled connection is reused only by a client with the same user, password, authSource, hosts and replica set (the password compared in constant time), so a client with a different password or authSource never inherits another login.

A harness sees each command's fixed name, outcome and server code, and each refusal's fixed reason, and never a filter, a collection name, a database name or a document. Without a harness nothing is reported and everything works.
The salted password is computed once per isolate and reused.

refusals.input: an aggregation pipeline with a $out or $merge stage
a filter, projection or pipeline using $where, $function or $accumulator, at any depth
refusals.reason: those operators run JavaScript on the server; a read-only client refuses them before anything is sent

refusals.input: an empty, over-long or special-character database or collection name
refusals.reason: names are validated before anything is sent

refusals.input: a mongodb+srv:// connection string, or a malformed one
refusals.reason: seed lists only: SRV needs DNS the Worker host does not do; the error says how to proceed

refusals.input: an aggregation returning more than MAX_AGGREGATE_DOCS
refusals.reason: the cursor is killed and the call refused rather than silently truncated

refusals.input: a password that is not ASCII
refusals.reason: SASLprep is not implemented, so the client refuses rather than authenticate wrongly

harness.secrets: Events are mzizi_harness::Event: static names, static keys and static string values only, so a filter, name or document cannot be formatted into one. The command name is one of a fixed list, else "other".

gaps: workers::Mongo (the pooled Worker client) does not yet take a harness; only Connection does.
No timing in events: the sans-IO core has no clock, so durations belong to the host's harness adapter.
A live connection from a deployed Worker to an Atlas cluster is verified by the consuming application, not by this crate's tests.
